chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a slave who put out the eye of a free man, while the slave had a debt, that upon the slave there is a prescribed liability for the one whose eye was put out, and the debt of the creditors is nullified.”

key_terms.الْمَفْقُوءِ: the one whose eye was put out
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule when an indebted slave put out the eye of a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a slave who destroyed the eye of a free man while the slave was indebted. It establishes the precedence of the injured party’s claim in this case and indicates the nullification of the creditors’ debt claims against the slave.
